pr_title: Don't call user callbacks on MsQuic worker thread.
pr_body:
Closes #98039.

This should also help with https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/55979, as previously the callbacks were delaying MsQuic threads which led to MsQuic thinking the workers were overloaded.

issue_context.title: QuicConnection: Validate certificates asynchronously.
issue_context.body:
https://github.com/microsoft/msquic/pull/3318 introduced new API for validating peer certificates asynchronously:

- Value of QUIC_STATUS_PENDING is returned when handling `PEER_CERTIFICATE_RECEIVED` event
- Later, use [`ConnectionCertificateValidationComplete`](https://github.com/microsoft/msquic/blob/feccf650c27746b9880f468aa2a8a34e1345ea73/docs/api/ConnectionCertificateValidationComplete.md) to set the result.

We would have to dispatch a Task to threadpool to do the actual validation, so this may slow down the handshake a bit (affecting time to first byte in HTTP/3), but might improve overall effectiveness as we don't block MsQuic threads while we download CRL or intermediate certificates for the actual chain building.

related to https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/79441. It may be beneficial if validation needs to do any IO.

This issue is only about an internal implementation detail, it does not touch public API and seems orthogonal to the issue you mentioned.

However, one thing that would be interesting to add is X509Chain.BuildAsync (here we actually do the sync-over-async of downloading the certs). But I am not sure if the API proposal would pass since AFAIK we can do it truly async only on Linux.

review_comments: once we update to 2.4, we can remove the `if` and change the `StartAsyncCertificateValidation` to `async void`.
Are we losing now the specific errors we were returning? Like discerning user_cancelled? Does it matter (affects the other side and what info they get), or not?

MsQuic does not use the specific error code value, it only checks for PENDING for async validation, SUCCESS for accept, and any error simply means reject.

With the async validation, we will actually be able to select the right TLS alert code which will go out over the wire, If the user validation callback throws, this will default to USER_CANCELLED as before, but if the callback returns false then it becomes BAD_CERTIFICATE. We can perhaps be more specific when no custom validation is present (there are alerts for stuff like UNTRUSTED_CERTIFICATE and similar) but I don't think we do that even in SslStream on some platforms.

The goal of QuicConnection.SslConnectionOptions was to separate certificate logic from the connection code. So that you can read this code like: "Ahh there is a cert validation logic, ok, let me get back to this if I need to". Now it's split over two places.
So please keep this event handler looking like it was.

The validation logic is still inside `QuicConnection.SslConnectionOptions`. The part that I moved to `QuicConnection` deals with copying data from the `PEER_CERTIFICATE_RECEIVED_DATA` so that it can be handed off to the threadpool.
